md_docs_2dependency-builds(3) Library Functions Manual md_docs_2dependency-builds(3)

NAME

md_docs_2dependency-builds - Dependency builds

Native builds normally use installed packages where supported. Configure with -DASCIICHAT_BUILD_DEPS_FROM_SOURCE=ON to exercise the source implementations of the converted dependencies. This still requires the platform SDK and packages for dependencies that do not have an upstream CMake build, including OpenSSL.

The source implementations use upstream CMake targets for PCRE2, Opus, zstd, zlib, PortAudio, FreeType, Expat, Abseil, miniupnpc, libdatachannel and its networking dependencies, libwebsockets, WebRTC AEC3, x265, mimalloc, and utf8proc. mdns uses its upstream interface target. FFTW, libuv and yyjson already use upstream CMake builds. libvterm has a small local target because upstream supplies a Makefile; its generated encoding tables are tracked build outputs.

FetchContent downloads pinned sources during configuration. The upstream targets compile when cmake --Build System runs, so Ninja handles their ordering, incremental rebuilds, compiler settings, include paths and transitive links. Upstream options are scoped to each dependency. Sources can be cached between configurations, while each build directory keeps its own generated files and objects.

ASCIICHAT_SHARED_DEPS=ON selects shared native dependencies; ASCIICHAT_SHARED_DEPS=OFF selects static source targets. WASM, iOS and musl retain their static dependency policy. AEC3's upstream components remain static and can be linked into either the shared ascii-chat library or an executable. CMake records the circular dependency between its factory and implementation, so consumers do not need whole-archive flags or hand-written archive lists.

FFmpeg and Fontconfig consume installed codec/font dependencies through pkg-config. Small staging targets install x265, FreeType and Expat into the build tree before those external builds run. This keeps their configure scripts out of the top-level configure step without replacing their supported upstream build systems. libsodium, OpenSSL, ALSA, x264, BearSSL and libexecinfo likewise retain their upstream build systems where source builds are required.

On Windows, native builds use Clang, Ninja and the Visual Studio SDK environment. CMake selects the MSVC-compatible C runtime for both application code and third-party DLLs. No SHELL environment override is required. WASM's remaining Autotools dependency, libsodium, uses Bash and Make from one MSYS2 installation; ASCIICHAT_MSYS2_ROOT can identify it when automatic discovery is insufficient. Windows shared builds select Abseil's upstream single DLL option, including when Clang uses its GNU-style command line with the MSVC ABI.

Testing source targets

The dependency smoke executable exercises compression round trips, an Opus encoder, PCRE2 compilation, FreeType, PortAudio metadata, UPnP, XML parsing, terminal allocation, Unicode widths, TLS/WebRTC library initialization, an AEC3 factory and mimalloc allocation. It does not open cameras, audio devices or network connections.

cmake -S tests/cmake/dependencies -B build/dependency-static -G Ninja \


  -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++ \


  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DASCIICHAT_SHARED_DEPS=OFF
cmake --build build/dependency-static
ctest --test-dir build/dependency-static --output-on-failure
cmake -S tests/cmake/dependencies -B build/dependency-shared -G Ninja \


  -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++ \


  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DASCIICHAT_SHARED_DEPS=ON
cmake --build build/dependency-shared
ctest --test-dir build/dependency-shared --output-on-failure

Set OPENSSL_ROOT_DIR when OpenSSL is outside the normal search paths. Windows must also be able to load its OpenSSL DLLs when running the smoke executable. The WASM build has a separate wasm-dependencies target and CTest entry.
